<!-- SOURCE_TURN_002_BEGIN -->
Sure, here's a revised curriculum that can be completed in 12 weeks, dedicating 10 hours per week:

Module 1: Introduction to Digital Product Design (10 hours)

* Overview of digital product design
* Principles of design thinking
* Understanding user-centered design
* Practical exercises to apply design thinking and user-centered design

Module 2: User Experience Design (UX) (10 hours)

* Understanding the user experience (UX) design process
* Developing user personas
* Creating user journey maps
* Wireframing and prototyping
* Practical exercises to apply UX design principles

Module 3: User Research (10 hours)

* Understanding user research methods and techniques
* Conducting user interviews
* Creating surveys and questionnaires
* Analyzing user data and feedback
* Practical exercises to apply user research methods

Module 4: User Interface Design (UI) (10 hours)

* Understanding user interface (UI) design principles
* Designing interfaces for mobile and web applications
* Using typography, color, and imagery in UI design
* Prototyping and testing UI designs
* Practical exercises to apply UI design principles

Module 5: Design Tools and Techniques (10 hours)

* Introduction to design software and tools
* Using graphic design tools for digital product design
* Creating design assets for digital products
* Design handoff and collaboration
* Practical exercises to use design software and tools

Module 6: Putting it All Together (10 hours)

* Applying all the principles and techniques learned throughout the curriculum
* Final project to create a digital product from start to finish
* Presenting and receiving feedback on the final project
* Practical exercises to refine the final project

This revised curriculum provides a comprehensive overview of digital product design and allows the learner to gain hands-on experience with each stage of the design process. The practical exercises throughout each module provide opportunities for the learner to apply the skills and techniques learned in each module. The final project in Module 6 allows the learner to apply all the skills and knowledge gained throughout the curriculum and showcase their ability to create a digital product from start to finish.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_002_END -->

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_008_BEGIN -->
Great idea! Here's a proposal for an online digital product design clinic for beginners:

Overview:
The online digital product design clinic is designed to provide beginner learners with practical, hands-on experience in digital product design. The clinic will simulate real-world projects to enable students to learn by doing. Students will work in teams to design digital products for clients with specific needs, goals, and requirements.

Structure:
The clinic will be structured into three phases: research, design, and testing. Each phase will last four weeks and will culminate in a deliverable that demonstrates the student's understanding and application of the beginner curriculum. At the end of the clinic, students will have completed a portfolio-worthy digital product design project.

Phase 1: Research (4 weeks)

* Students will be divided into teams and assigned a client with specific needs and requirements.
* Students will conduct user research to gain a deep understanding of the target audience, market trends, and user needs.
* Students will create user personas, user journey maps, and conduct a competitive analysis.
* Students will present their research findings to the client and receive feedback.

Phase 2: Design (4 weeks)

* Students will use their research findings to ideate, sketch, and create wireframes for their digital product design.
* Students will create user flows, sitemaps, and design mockups.
* Students will present their design solutions to the client and receive feedback.
* Students will iterate on their design solutions based on client feedback.

Phase 3: Testing (4 weeks)

* Students will conduct usability testing to validate their design solutions.
* Students will create high-fidelity prototypes and conduct user testing.
* Students will refine their design solutions based on user testing feedback.
* Students will present their final design solutions to the client.

Delivery:
The online digital product design clinic will be delivered through a learning management system (LMS) that includes instructional videos, readings, assignments, and quizzes. Each phase will include weekly team meetings with a mentor who will provide guidance, support, and feedback on students' work. The final deliverable will be a portfolio-worthy digital product design project that students can use to showcase their skills and experience.

Benefits:
The online digital product design clinic offers a collaborative and practical learning environment that enables students to apply their beginner curriculum knowledge to real-world projects. By working on a project with a client, students will learn how to communicate with clients, manage project timelines, and work in a team. Additionally, students will have a portfolio-worthy project to showcase their skills to potential employers.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_008_END -->

### Chinese translation — EDIT HERE

<!-- ZH_TURN_008_BEGIN -->
好主意！以下是为初学者设计的在线数字产品设计诊所的提案：

概述：
在线数字产品设计诊所旨在为初学者提供数字产品设计方面的实践性、动手经验。该诊所将模拟现实世界的项目，使学生能够通过实践学习。学生将分组为具有特定需求、目标和要求的客户设计数字产品。

结构：
该诊所将分为三个阶段：研究、设计和测试。每个阶段将持续四周，并以一个展示学生对初级课程理解和应用的交付成果结束。在诊所结束时，学生将完成一个值得放入作品集的数字产品设计项目。

阶段1：研究（4周）

* 学生将被分成小组，并分配一个具有特定需求和要求的客户。
* 学生将进行用户研究，以深入了解目标受众、市场趋势和用户需求。
* 学生将创建用户画像、用户旅程地图，并进行竞争分析。
* 学生将向客户展示他们的研究发现并接收反馈。

阶段2：设计（4周）

* 学生将利用他们的研究发现进行构思、草图绘制，并为他们的数字产品设计创建线框图。
* 学生将创建用户流程、站点地图和设计模型。
* 学生将向客户展示他们的设计方案并接收反馈。
* 学生将根据客户反馈迭代他们的设计方案。

阶段3：测试（4周）

* 学生将进行可用性测试以验证他们的设计方案。
* 学生将创建高保真原型并进行用户测试。
* 学生将根据用户测试反馈完善他们的设计方案。
* 学生将向客户展示他们的最终设计方案。

交付方式：
在线数字产品设计诊所将通过一个学习管理系统（LMS）交付，该系统包括教学视频、阅读材料、作业和测验。每个阶段将包括每周与导师的团队会议，导师将提供指导、支持和反馈。最终交付成果将是一个值得放入作品集的数字产品设计项目，学生可以用它来展示他们的技能和经验。

好处：
在线数字产品设计诊所提供了一个协作和实用的学习环境，使学生能够将他们的初级课程知识应用于现实世界的项目。通过与客户合作项目，学生将学习如何与客户沟通、管理项目时间表以及团队合作。此外，学生将拥有一个值得放入作品集的项目，向潜在雇主展示他们的技能。
